messages.body_plain:
I'm using reshape2 to melt a datafrmae and then recast it.  My
datafrmae contains columns of date time stamps in POSIXct format.
dcast seems to turn those POSIXct values into numeric equivalents.  Is
this a bug or am I missing something ?

Example code below

names(airquality) <- tolower(names(airquality))

airquality$datestamp<-as.POSIXct(strftime(paste("2011-",airquality
$month,"-" ,airquality$day, sep="")))

aqm <- melt(airquality, id=c("month", "day", "datestamp"), na.rm=TRUE)

dcast(aqm, day + month ~ variable)

dcast(aqm, datestamp ~ variable)

aqm <- melt(airquality, id=c("month", "day"), na.rm=TRUE)

dcast(aqm, day + month ~ variable)

> dcast(aqm, day + month ~ variable)

day month ozone solar.r wind temp datestamp

1 1 5 41 190 7.4 67 1304204400

2 1 6 NA 286 8.6 78 1306882800
........

Thanks,

Paul.

messages.body_plain:
Hi:

On Fri, Sep 2, 2011 at 3:18 PM, PaulHurleyUK <pa...@paulhurley.co.uk> wrote:
> I'm using reshape2 to melt a datafrmae and then recast it.  My
> datafrmae contains columns of date time stamps in POSIXct format.
> dcast seems to turn those POSIXct values into numeric equivalents.  Is
> this a bug or am I missing something ?
>
> Example code below
>
> names(airquality) <- tolower(names(airquality))
>
> airquality$datestamp<-as.POSIXct(strftime(paste("2011-",airquality
> $month,"-" ,airquality$day, sep="")))
>
> aqm <- melt(airquality, id=c("month", "day", "datestamp"), na.rm=TRUE)
>
> dcast(aqm, day + month ~ variable)
>
> dcast(aqm, datestamp ~ variable)

All is fine up to here. Notice that you've kept datestamp as an id
variable so that it retains its class when melted and casted.

>
> aqm <- melt(airquality, id=c("month", "day"), na.rm=TRUE)

Now datestamp is treated as a(n implicit) measure variable, so its
values get coerced to numeric (along with those of ozone, solar.r,
etc.) during the melt process. value and variable are atomic objects
in the data frame aqm, which means they can only have one class.
Hence, when the values of datestamp are combined with those of the
other four measure variables to form the new, stacked variable
'value', its values get coerced to numeric so that the class of value
returns numeric. Consequently, when you  cast this version of aqm,
datestamp is now numeric rather than POSIXct. This is a
well-documented feature of R when atomic objects are combined; here is
a simple, basic example:

# ---------- (digression)
> a <- letters[1:3]
> b <- 4:6
> class(a)
[1] "character"
> class(b)
[1] "integer"
> d <- c(a, b)
> class(d)
[1] "character"
> d
[1] "a" "b" "c" "4" "5" "6"

Since atomic objects can only have one class, the integer values in b,
when combined with the character values in a, are coerced to be of
class character, since integer values can be converted to character
but not vice versa.
#-------------
You can always coerce back into a Date or POSIXct class:

u <- as.Date(aqc$datestamp/86400, origin = '1970-01-01')
> head(u)
[1] "2011-05-01" "2011-06-01" "2011-07-01" "2011-08-01" "2011-09-01"
[6] "2011-05-02"

v <- as.POSIXct(aqc$datestamp, origin = '1970-01-01')
> head(v)
[1] "2011-05-01 08:00:00 PDT" "2011-06-01 08:00:00 PDT"
[3] "2011-07-01 08:00:00 PDT" "2011-08-01 08:00:00 PDT"
[5] "2011-09-01 08:00:00 PDT" "2011-05-02 08:00:00 PDT"

The time zone is local unless you change it with the tz = argument of
as.POSIXct().

HTH,
Dennis

messages.subject: ddply and spliited_r conserving .variable order?
messages.body_plain:
Hi

I am doing a ddply operation, where my "by" variable is an ordered
factor. I would like ddply to return the results according to the
order of this factor, but it seems unfortunately ddply is returning
results according to alphabetical order of the factor instead.

is there a way to change this easily? I mean, specifying the order in
which .(variable) will execute the function?

Here is my application: I have a data frame that where say I will want
to have first woman appearing, than men. I use ddply to create on top
of each category some total stat:

dd<-data.frame(sex=factor(c(rep("Women",3), rep("Men",7)),
ordered=TRUE),ind=c(paste("Women", 1:3), paste("Men", 1:7)), val=1:10)

addGroupMean<-function(df){
  mean<-numcolwise(sum)(df)
  nam <- paste("group", unique(as.character(df$sex )))
  ret<-data.frame(sex=nam, ind=NA,val=mean)
  rbind(ret,df)
}
ddply(dd, .(sex), addGroupMean)

Unfortunately, ddply did not return the variables in the order of the
variable! Any idea how to solve this?

Thanks

messages.body_plain:
here is one solution that I came up with that might be able to be integrated with plyr in general.  I hacked rlply to capture and store the seed of every iteration in foreach, then format them as a data frame that is stored as an attribute, similar to what plyr does with splitting labels.  This data frame could then be stored for easy replication of the simulation.  The problem with this solution is that the default random number generator is the Mersene twister that holds a random seed of length 626.  holding that for each replication might get too large.  I show it with the simplest random number generator.  It's not quite the same as setting the seed, but gets us closer.

---
> library(plyr)
> library(doMC)
> registerDoMC(9)
>
> my.rlply <- function(.n, .expr, .progress = "none", .parallel=F) {
+   if (is.function(.expr)) {
+     f <- .expr
+   } else {
+     f <- eval.parent(substitute(function(){
+ ._rng.seed_<-.Random.seed
+ structure({.expr},"._rng.seed_" =._rng.seed_)
+ }))
+   }
+
+   progress <- create_progress_bar(.progress)
+   result <- vector("list", length = .n)
+
+   progress$init(.n)
+   on.exit(progress$term())
+
+ if(.parallel){
+ if(!require("foreach")) stop("foreach package required for parallel plyr operation", call. = FALSE)
+ if(getDoParWorkers()==1) warning("No Parallel Backend Registered", call.=TRUE)
+ result <- foreach(i= seq_len(.n)) %dopar% f()
+ seeds  <- laply(result, attr, "._rng.seed_")
+ result <- llply(result, `attr<-`, '._rng.seed_',NULL)
+ result <- structure(result, seeds=seeds)
+   } else for(i in seq_len(.n)) {
+     result[i] <- list(f())
+     progress$step()
+   }
+   result
+ }
>
> RNGkind("Wichmann-Hill")
> l<-my.rlply(3, rnorm(4),.parallel=T)
> ldply(l, attr, '._rng.seed_')
data frame with 0 columns and 0 rows

out.file <- file('transposed.txt', 'w')

I have an iMac with Lion (10.7.1) pre-installed and am trying to use
the plyr .parallel argument. Given Hadley's earlier statement that
multicore is the only backend working with plyr currently, I have
verified that the multicore itself is working using the script below.
In the second part of the script, I tried to use plyr. There is an
effect, but it is not a good one. I ran the code as a batch job. The
script and the log (which shows timings and software versions) are
below. Have I misunderstood something or is there something I am doing
wrong?

Thanks!
Eric

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

library ( foreach)
library ( multicore)
library ( doMC)
library ( plyr)
ls()

registerDoMC(cores = 6)

# Slight variation on the Steve Weston "Getting Started with doMC and
foreach" example:

x <- iris[which(iris[, 5] != "setosa"), c(1, 5)]
trials <- 5000
multi_ptime <- system.time({
	r <- foreach(icount(trials), .combine = cbind) %dopar% {
		ind <- sample(400, 400, replace = TRUE)
		result1 <- glm(x[ind, 2] ~ x[ind, 1], family = binomial(logit))
		coefficients(result1)
		}
	})

single_ptime <- system.time({
	r <- foreach(icount(trials), .combine = cbind) %do% {
		ind <- sample(400, 400, replace = TRUE)
		result1 <- glm(x[ind, 2] ~ x[ind, 1], family = binomial(logit))
		coefficients(result1)
		}
	})

print (multi_ptime)
print (single_ptime)

# Decent speedup.

# A set of random-junk data

trials <- 200000
abc.df <- data.frame ( a = rnorm ( trials  ), b = rnorm ( trials   ),
c = rnorm ( trials   ) )
# Add a Group variable
abc.df <- transform ( abc.df, G = sample (1:12, size = trials   ,
replace = TRUE ) )

abc.df, .fun = transform , abcSinExp = sin(exp ( a + b + c)) ) )
p6time <- system.time ( res6P <- ddply ( .variables = "G", .data =
abc.df, .fun = transform , abcSinExp = sin(exp ( a + b + c))  ,
.parallel = TRUE ) )

there is a point where the task you are paralleling is so fast that the
overhead to parallel winds up taking more time than the task itself.

try using your junk data with an lm call or a more complex function and you'll see a good increase.

system.time(ddply(dat,.(x),function(df) Sys.sleep(df$y),.parallel=F))

messages.subject: should plyr::rename give an error when trying to rename an inexistent name?
messages.subject_clean: should plyr::rename give an error when trying to rename an inexistent name?
messages.body_plain:
I would find it helpful if plyr::rename gave an error when the name
that I am trying to change does not exist, as this would likely mean
that I mistyped the name. Perhaps I'm missing a more common scenario.
If not by default, it would be nice to have an option.

example:
should the following give an error?
rename(mtcars, c("dispxx" = "displ"))

I patched the old rename function before I realized there is a new
one. I'll paste it here in case Hadley thinks it's a good idea and
wants to add it to legacy reshape:
rename_old <- function (x, replace)
{
    replacement <- replace[names(x)]
    if(!(sum(!is.na <http://is.na>(replacement)) == length(replace))) {
        not_found <- names(replace)[!(names(replace) %in% names(x))]
        stop("error, the following names do not exist in
",substitute(x),": ",paste(not_found,collapse=", "))
    }
    names(x)[!is.na <http://is.na>(replacement)] <- replacement[!is.na <http://is.na>(replacement)]
    x
}

Scott

messages.body_plain:
Hi Joe,

I think the cleanest way is to use substitute to build up the formula:

llply(1:2, function(i) {
  yvar <- as.name <http://as.name>(paste("y", i, sep = ""))
  f <- eval(substitute(y ~ x, list(y = yvar)))
  lm(f, data = dfr)
})

Hadley

> dfr<-
> data.frame(i=rep(letters[1:3],each=5),y1=rnorm(15),y2=rnorm(15),x=rnorm(15))
>
> # First, say I just want to run regression of y1~x for each level of i
>
> #This works
> lm2<-function(junk) lm(y1~x, data=dfr) # junk not used
> dlply(dfr,.(i),lm2)
> # (note: function() lm(y1~x, data=dfr) does not work in dlply)
>
> #This works (but will of course not reference dfr in the o/p)
> lm1<-function(y1,x,...) lm(y1~x)
> dlply(dfr,.(i),splat(lm1))
>
> #But suppose I want to vary the dependent variable, for example maybe

> #   maybe y2 later
> lm3<-function(resp,x) lm(resp~x, data=dfr)

messages.subject_clean: column names for summarize with multiple values
messages.body_plain:
Summarize has useful behavior in various cases when a variable is not atomic:

test <- data.frame(a=1:10,b=1:10 %/% 3)
rng <- function(a) c(min=min(a),max=max(a))  # range with labels

Multiple columns from one variable:

> ddply(test,.(b),summarize,r=t(rng(a)))
  b r.1 r.2
1 0   1   2
2 1   3   5
...

Useful result, but it would be nice if the labels were r.min and r.max, the way data.frame does it:

> data.frame(r=t(rng(1)))
  r.min r.max
1     1     1

and maybe even min and max if there is no "r=", again like data.frame:

> data.frame(t(rng(1)))
  min max
1   1   1

If r is a vector rather than a matrix, ddply gives multiple rows in the result (with no labels).  This isn't documented; is it intentional?

> ddply(test,.(b),summarize,r=rng(a))
  b  r
1 0  1
2 0  2
...

I would think it would be more useful if the rows were labelled, but maybe that's getting too far into DWIM <http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DWIM> territory, something like this:

  b r.name <http://r.name>  r
1 0    min  1
2 0    max  2
3 1    min  3
